title: Mirror Frequency Distance
summary: Given a string s consisting of lowercase English letters and digits, for each unique character c in the string: - Determine its mirror character m , where: - For letters, the mirror of c is the letter at the same position from the end of the alphabet.
statement: Given a string s consisting of lowercase English letters and digits, for each unique character c in the string: - Determine its mirror character m , where: - For letters, the mirror of c is the letter at the same position from the end of the alphabet. - For digits, the mirror of c is the digit at the same position from the end of the range '0' to '9'. - Compute the absolute difference between the frequency of c and the frequency of m , denoted as |freq(c) - freq(m)| . - Sum these differences for all distinct mirror pairs, ensuring each pair is counted only once. Return the total sum of these values.
constraints: s contains lowercase letters and decimal digits.
Letter mirrors are a↔z, b↔y, and so on; digit mirrors are 0↔9, 1↔8, and so on.
For each mirror pair, add the absolute frequency difference exactly once.
reference_solution:
def mirror_frequency_distance(s):
    from collections import Counter
    counts=Counter(s);seen=set();answer=0
    for character in counts:
        other=chr(219-ord(character)) if character.isalpha() else str(9-int(character))
        if character in seen:continue
        seen.add(character);seen.add(other);answer+=abs(counts[character]-counts[other])
    return answer

hints: Mirroring is an involution, so characters form disjoint pairs.
Count all characters, then visit each encountered pair only if neither side was handled.
Add the absolute difference and mark both characters seen.
Every pair is counted once, including a missing mirror through its zero default frequency.

a and z have equal frequency, so their pair contributes zero.
